Commentary.Commentary: Right then, another night where the ball dominated the bat to an extent given how good a surface this was to bat on and this time, it was England who were able to take advantage of the batting frailties. Next up, the caravan moves to Pune for the 4th T20I and a crucial one at that. That game will be played on Friday, 31 January and will begin at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT) but you can join us a lot sooner for the build-up. Till then, take care and goodbye!

Varun Chakravarthy is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his brilliant five-wicket haul and rarely does it happen that a player from the losing team. Says that he is sad that they didn't win this game but it is the nature of the game and they will look to move on. Adds that when you are playing for the country, you need to take accountability and hopes to improve further. On his bowling spells, he says that he is mentally ready to bowl whenever required. Adds that he has been working on a flipper which is coming out nicely.

Jos Buttler, the victorious skipper of England says the pacers bowled really well and showed they can vary pace too. Lauds Adil Rashid's performance and says he is happy to have somebody like him on the team. He then goes on to appreciate the way Ben Duckett played on what was a sticky pitch. Says they lost wickets in clusters which was not ideal but they managed to get to a total and then pick early wickets which was a key. Credits Adil Rashid and Mark Wood for putting on that last wicket partnership.

Suryakumar Yadav, the captain of India says that he felt there would be a bit of dew later on and with the batters in the middle, he thought the match was still in their hands. Credits Adil Rashid for the way he bowled in the middle phase and didn't allow them to rotate the strike. Mentions that you always learn something from a T20 game and he thinks that they conceded a few too many runs in the end and from a batting point of view as well, they will go back to the drawing board. On Mohammed Shami, he says that it is good to see him back in the middle and is hopeful that he will improve further. Ends by saying that he will tell Varun Chakravarthy to keep doing what he is doing and chuckles by saying that he is hopeful that he will score some more runs in the next game.
The Presentation ceremony...

Adil Rashid is now down for a chat. He says as a team they bowled exceptionally well and on his wicket of Tilak Varma, he says the ball gripped and turned nicely to go through. Mentions that he puts in a lot of effort in the nets and has learned a lot with experience. Says that they as a bowling unit made use of the variations in pace nicely and his last wicket partnership with Mark Wood was only to try and add as much as possible.

Earlier in the game, Suryakumar Yadav asked England to bat first on what looked like a flat track and everyone expected big runs. However, Phil Salt once again flopped at the top but this time, Ben Duckett was able to hit his way out of trouble alongside skipper Jos Buttler. In the middle overs, it was a similar story from the previous games as Varun Chakravarthy ripped through the English batting lineup. Liam Livingstone did well to get those big hits away once the wickets started to tumble and a solid final-wicket stand between Rashid and Wood saw England notch up 171 runs which actually proved to be quite crucial. In reply, we saw a solid bowling performance, this time from England and they picked up enough wickets in the middle phase to be able to press the issue later on and get the win.

India and their spinners have been dominant in the first couple of matches but in this game and the last one, we have also seen their flaws with the bat. The no-holds-barred approach at the top is certainly exciting but once you lose more than a couple of wickets in the Powerplay, the pressure starts to tell. Abhishek Sharma got off to a flier before getting out and the rest of the top order didn't have much of an impact. It was then Washington Sundar and Hardik Pandya who tried to steady the ship but after a sluggish stand, Sundar fell. Axar Patel then walked in and it was a similar story and despite a few hits from the bat of Pandya, India lost wickets in a heap at the death and were well beaten in the end.

Disciplined and controlled aggression from the English pacers this evening and they have managed to defend the runs on the board after coming close and being unable to get over the line in the last game. The tone was set up top by Jofra Archer, Mark Wood and Brydon Carse who picked up a wicket each. Then it was Adil Rashid who ruled the middle phase, picking up the crucial wicket of Tilak Varma and put a cap on the runs which allowed the pacers to take advantage of. Carse showed solidity yet again but it was Jamie Overton who was able to turn an underwhelming tour thus far into something meaningful and picked up 3 wickets.

The series is well and truly alive and England have come roaring back with a solid performance in the field! 171 seemed well below par but they have made huge amends with the ball and India's middle-order woes have been on display here too. India lead the series 2-1 heading into the final two games, and we might see a photo finish to this five-match series.

Commentary.Commentary: Comes into the attack and fires the first one, full, on middle, Tilak Varma walks down to the pitch of the ball and knocks it to long on for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Liam Livingstone to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A dot to end the over and the Powerplay! England chipped 3 wickets in it. This is on a hard length, over off, Hardik Pandya taps it out to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Mark Wood to Hardik Pandya, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, angled into the batter, Hardik Pandya drops it in front of point and looks for a run but is denied.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Mark Wood to Hardik Pandya, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes full and attacks the stumps, Tilak Varma taps it to mid on and takes a quick run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Mark Wood to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard, on a back of a length, over middle, Tilak Varma dabs it out to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Mark Wood to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Angling in, down leg, Tilak Varma plays inside the line and misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Mark Wood to Tilak Varma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length, on off, Hardik Pandya works it past backward point for a single and gets off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Mark Wood to Hardik Pandya, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hardik Pandya is the new batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Mark Wood comes back into the attack and makes an immediate impact. India in some sort of trouble now at 48/3 as they lose their skipper. Wood goes full pace and hits the deck on a length, angling it into leg, Suryakumar Yadav looks to flick it behind but gets a top edge that goes very high in the night sky but just as far as the keeper to his left. Phil Salt settles under it and takes the simple catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Phil Salt b Mark Wood
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Mark Wood to Suryakumar Yadav, OUT! c Phil Salt b Mark Wood.

Commentary.Commentary: Ends the over well, does Archer but 13 runs come off it. Fuller in length on middle, angled in, Varma gets low and nudges it away back onto the deck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Jofra Archer to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Around the wicket now, bowled full and wide outside off, in the blockhole, Varma drives it square but straight to cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Jofra Archer to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Finally, Archer goes pace on, bowling it on a hard length over middle, SKY punches it wide of mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Archer is just bowling slower balls to SKY at the moment. Too short and wide, Yadav gets up on his toes and cuts it up and over point for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good-length delivery, on middle and leg, another leg cutter, Yadav tucks it away neatly through mid-wicket and picks up a couple of quick runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! That's a signature shot from Suryakumar Yadav. Jofra Archer looks to take pace off and bowls a leg cutter on the leg peg, SKY gets across and under it before lifting it over fine leg for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Crunched away! Banged in short and wide, Varma gives the charge and backs away a bit before slapping it hard and through the point region for a boundary. 12 runs and a wicket in that over, entertaining stuff!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Brydon Carse to Tilak Varma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length, angling it across middle and leg, Tilak Varma nudges it away to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Brydon Carse to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tilak Varma walks out to bat at number 4 for India. Oh dear, Jamie Smith, who did have a calf strain before the game, is now seen leaving the field. Jacob Bethell comes in as a replacement while Phil Salt gears up to keep the wickets.

OUT! CAUGHT! That is a fine, fine catch from Jofra Archer and both Indian batters are now back in the hut. Brydon Carse hits the deck hard and bowls it at the stumps, Abhishek Sharma comes down the pitch and backs away to open up the off side but ends up skiing it a mile high and over extra cover. Jofra Archer at mid off circles around the high ball and seems to have just misjudged it in the end but manages to leap behind him and reverse-cup it wonderfully. Sharma departs for 24 off 14 and India now 31/2.
Commentary.Howout: c Jofra Archer b Brydon Carse
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Brydon Carse to Abhishek Sharma, OUT! c Jofra Archer b Brydon Carse.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Oh, just timed beautifully! The attempted yorker on middle turns out to be a full toss and Abhishek Sharma is taken aback. However, Sharma pushes at it and the ball speeds away wide of mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Brydon Carse to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Just back of a length, over middle and leg, too tight to pull and Abhishek Sharma is beaten all ends up.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Brydon Carse to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Flashes and flashes hard does Sharma! Carse begins with a hard-length ball around off, Sharma keeps a stable base and looks to go over mid off but gets a top edge that flies over short third and into the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Brydon Carse to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good-length delivery, attacking middle and leg stump, Suryakumar Yadav sets up to go big but then just decides to block it toward mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a slightly dragged length and angled into the body, Sharma waits back and just dabs it down, late and behind point for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! That is some shot! Hard length around the top of off, at 145 clicks, Abhishek Sharma just stays put and nonchalantly drives it flat over extra cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Shorter in length and angled down the leg side from around the wicket, Sharma misses the pull and a wide is called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length around the fifth stump line, Suryakumar Yadav hangs back and angles it away through backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Suryakumar Yadav, the Indian skipper walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT! Sanju Samson departs via a short delivery again and England have their first wicket. Jofra Archer just strolls in and bangs in a short ball over middle at 145.7 kph and gets the ball to hurry through. Samson camps back and backs away to pull it over long on but mistimes it badly. The ball goes just over mid on where Adil Rashid just takes a few steps back and takes a simple catch. India 16/1!
Commentary.Howout: c Adil Rashid b Jofra Archer
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Jofra Archer to Sanju Samson, OUT! c Adil Rashid b Jofra Archer.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard and bowls it in the channel around off, Sharma hangs back and punches it square through point and the ball pings off the bat to deep point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and over off, cutting back in a touch, Samson looks to punch it away but gets an inside edge onto the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Mark Wood to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Hard length again, quick too but slips down the leg side for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Mark Wood to Sanju Samson, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Banged in on a hard length again, on off and angling in at almost 149 clicks, Samson watchfully blocks it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Mark Wood to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Up in the air...lands safely! Bowled from around the wicket, on a hard length and wide outside off, Sharma goes after it and gets a top edge that flies wide of deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Mark Wood to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Much more in control this time! Bowled at 150.5 kph, banged in a bit and over middle and leg, Sharma just leans back a touch and swats it up and well over mid on for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Mark Wood to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and away! Wood goes full and wide outside off at 150 clicks, Abhishek Sharma just throws his hands at it and manages to slice it over the cover region and it rolls away into the fence for the first boundary of the chase.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Mark Wood to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length, straighter again at the pads, tucked away neatly to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Mark Wood to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Wayward to begin with! Banged in a bit short, angling into the batter but this one angles down leg for a wide. England looking to cramp the batters for room early on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Mark Wood to Sanju Samson, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Mark Wood to share the attack from the other end.
Tidy start from Archer, just 3 off it! A well-directed bumper, right around the front shoulder, Samson gets a touch low and just angles the pull down to fine leg for one more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Jofra Archer to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length and angled well into the pads, Sharma clips it away off the pads and wide of deep fine leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on a tight line around off, angling in, Sharma gets on his toes and punches it square towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Gives the charge but is well beaten! Banged in on a hard length over off at over 144 clicks again, Abhishek Sharma comes down the pitch and swings across the line but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Around the wicket to the left-hander, bowled on a hard length in the channel at 144.3 clicks, Abhishek Sharma stays upright and pushes it down to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Off the mark right away! Archer begins on the shorter side and angles it in at the hips, Sanju Samson whips it away down to fine leg and picks up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Jofra Archer to Sanju Samson, 1 run.
